messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock down the OTel/Prom label contract for runtime -> infra metrics before the dashboards sprint. @sam @priya can you confirm overlaps?

sam: yep, saw the doc draft. main gaps: (1) 'route' label cardinality, (2) model vs model_family naming, (3) consistent env/region tags.

priya: +1. also want to avoid free-form tags from runtime libs — we need an allowlist.

maya: proposal from runtime team (sketch):
```
metric: llm.request.latency_ms
service.name: redwood-runtime
labels:
  env: prod|staging|qa
  region: us-east-1|eu-west-1
  model_family: gptx-3|redwood-1|...   # low-cardinality
  model_version: rdl-1.2-q4  # optional, higher-cardinality
  route_id: r_12345            # low-cardinality identifier for routing rule
  route_label: customer-visible-route-name  # optional, high-cardinality (use sparingly)
```

maya: idea is: dashboards/alerts should rely only on low-cardinality labels. route_label exists for debugging traces only.

lee: question — how are we ensuring SDKs don't accidentally set arbitrary tags?

priya: runtime SDK will only emit the allowlist keys. anything else goes into resource.attributes on the trace, not as metric labels.

sam: on prometheus ingestion side, we should run a label-cardinality guard that rejects >N distinct values for a metric/label combo in a window. eng-sre already has a prototype.

anika: infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-9832 for prometheus cardinality guard prototype deployment :robot_face:

infra-bot: INFRA-9832 created and assigned to eng-sre.

maya: for naming conventions — prefer dots for metric namespace (llm.request.*) and underscores for label keys. keeps Prom and OTel mapping straightforward.

priya: agree. also suggest canonical prefix for runtime metrics: redwood.runtime.* for infra-facing metrics, llm.* for product-facing.

sam: alerting rules: keep them on aggregated metrics like p95/p99 per model_family+region, not per-route_id. per-route alerts are noisy.

lee: dashboard owners — runtime team to own raw metrics and dashboards that show per-route sampling. eng-platform to own the product-facing dashboards (cost/latency slices). eng-sre owns alerts and cardinality monitoring.

maya: owners noted. next steps: (1) runtime team to land allowlist + SDK changes by end of next week (2) eng-platform to draft dashboard templates using only low-cardinality labels (3) eng-sre to roll out cardinality guard in canary env.

sam: I'll add PR template that enforces adding label schema to any metric PR.

priya: I'll drop a short doc into the repo with examples and the allowlist YAML.

lee: tiny UX ask for console: add a dropdown with model_family + region as default breakdowns, and an "advanced" option to pick route_id (read-only for admins).

maya: love that — @anika can you surface that to the console roadmap?

anika: noted, adding a console work item CON-2147.

maya: one last thing — can we agree on a quick naming cheat-sheet we can paste into PRs? I can draft.

sam: please do. keep it to one short table + example metrics.

priya: and let's schedule a 30-min cross-team sync after PRs land to sanity-check dashboards.

maya: agreed. thanks everyone.

maya: action items summary:
- runtime: implement allowlist + SDK changes (due +7d)
- eng-platform: dashboard templates + console dropdown spec (due +10d)
- eng-sre: deploy cardinality guard to canary (due +14d)
- sam: PR template change
- priya: add allowlist YAML doc
- anika: create console work item CON-2147

maya: ping me if anything slips. :thumbsup:
